posts.name: Raccoonoo
posts.cooked:
I'm not going to say that my players are awful at diplomacy, but when presented with the option of either making peace with someone who is punching them or continuing to punch back until that person is defeated, they tend to pick the second option.

That said, in Prime Wardens #86, if Haka gets impatient and starts beating the stuffing out of them and their new friend Tempest, in all likelihood, they aren't going to continue to try and talk her down. This is... problematic, because the pdf doesn't tell me how to run Haka if she's a threat. What dice do I roll? How many hits can she take? Do I just make her a D12 Lieutenant?

Basically, what should I do if my players want to straight up fight Haka?

posts.name: speedyolrac
posts.cooked:
If they don't wanna talk it is fine. they can lose out on that, but the game will not continue long enough for that to come into effect.

I think the official is rolling the environment and make her actions of that. I Would just roll whatever dice I want and make her do whatever. They do not have the power to stop her physically, and she cannot be killed. If they only speak in fist fights make sure she hits them hard enough to make then think about talking.  One can also say she ignores all their attack for they are too weak. It might be though but this might be a good teaching moment.

posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
I'd have a hard time justifying "the heroes cannot win this fight."  She's tough, but standing up the the whole Freedom Five+Unity at once?  I don't think so.  Especially since we'll have full stats for her when the full game comes out.

I'm thinking what I'd do is make her a "phantom" full villain with "real" HP.  Except that she just soaks the damage, takes out Tempest at the earliest opportunity, and then the next scene begins with her still hostile.  If the heroes attempt to defend her at any sort of risk to themselves, that counts as her "convince her to listen" the first time and then "convince her the heroes aren't villains" the second time.  If, after the battle, the heroes still persist in attacking her, she tries to flee.  If the heroes pursue her... well, only Legacy and Tachyon have a chance of doing so, and that fight she can win, especially when they're weakened by the spirit battle.

posts.cooked: For those Punch first, ask question later. I would let the hero develop some bonding time with Tempest, let the Heros and tempest fight off a few dinos before letting Haka in the scene. I would let Haka be very Vocal and very emotional. To her Tempest is Dawn, let the Heroes know that and how horrible Dawn is. Your group may fail at this and it is ok. Failure is part of comics.
